title: Change Data Capture: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Change Data Capture: Visual Guide

1. Two Ways To Watch | log-based and query-based CDC side by side on deletes, intermediate states, transactions, load and failure mode | query-based CDC is lesson 2's high-water mark pointed at a table and inherits its leaks; log-based is lesson 4's event stream with the log position as the event id

2. What Polling Misses | three row changes against a sliding poll interval, showing which transitions ever reach the consumer | polling returns current state, so any value overwritten before the next poll never existed downstream — shortening the interval lowers the odds but never the possibility

3. The Version Guard | four out-of-order events for one customer, including a redelivery and a stale delete, applied with and without a per-key version guard | storing the last applied version per key fixes ordering and makes redelivery idempotent in one comparison — and the tombstone must keep its version or a stale update resurrects the row

4. Snapshot Handoff | the four steps of joining a baseline snapshot to the live stream, and the failure each one hides | overlap between snapshot and stream is harmless with idempotent upserts; the real failure is directional — a snapshot row landing after a newer change rolls the record back
